Posterior-anterior putamen gradient changes differed according to subsequent remission status, with changes in the right putamen gradient predicting relapse. Striatal gradient changes were also associated with goal-directed and habitual behaviour during the slip-of-action task, response consistency during delay discounting, and circulating ghrelin and desacyl ghrelin concentrations. These findings identify longitudinal putamen reorganization as a candidate marker of vulnerability to relapse and link striatal plasticity to reward-related and metabolic processes in AN.

items.title_en: Multimodal Prediction of Distressing and Persistent Psychotic-Like Experiences in Adolescence across Environment, Genetics, and Neuroimaging
items.title_zh: 基于环境、遗传和神经影像的多模态预测青少年痛苦且持续的精神病样体验
items.abstract_en: Adolescent psychotic-like experiences, particularly those that are distressing and persistent (dpPLEs), may elevate risk for a range of psychiatric disorders, yet the relative predictive contributions of brain structure, genetics, and environment to dpPLEs remain unknown. Using four timepoints from 7,399 children in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, we developed stacked ensemble machine-learning models integrating cortical morphometry and whole-brain microstructural properties, polygenic risk scores, family psychiatric history, and childhood environmental factors to predict adolescent dpPLEs. Environmental predictors alone, driven by area deprivation index, neighborhood drug-related crime, and cumulative early adversity, were the strongest predictive domain (ROC-AUC = 0.687 {+/-} 0.003), outperforming genetic (0.619 {+/-} 0.020) and all imaging models (0.588-0.650). Adding genetic risk to environmental features produced the best-performing model overall (ROC-AUC = 0.697 {+/-} 0.007), whereas adding neuroimaging yielded no further incremental gain (ROC-AUC=0.683-0.696). Beyond environmental exposures, family history of psychosis, cross-disorder polygenic risk, and both globally distributed and regionally specific imaging components contributed to prediction. Childhood environmental factors thus capture a core predictive signal preceding dpPLEs, while genetic and neuroimaging features added comparatively modest discriminative prediction value, but may offer complementary biological insights.

items.title_en: Systematic evaluation of semantic similarity across language models for schizophrenia spectrum disorders
items.title_zh: 针对精神分裂症谱系障碍的跨语言模型语义相似性系统评估
items.abstract_en: Background: Semantic similarity features derived from language embeddings have been proposed as markers of schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), but prior studies have reported inconsistent directions of effect and limited evidence regarding their relationship to specific dimensions of thought and language disturbance. We systematically evaluated how language model architecture and preprocessing strategy influence semantic similarity signals in SSD. Methods: Speech samples from 228 participants (152 SSD, 76 healthy volunteers) were analyzed using six embedding models: GloVe, LSA, Word2Vec, RoBERTa, GPT-2, and Llama. Semantic similarity features were computed across three preprocessing levels (verbatim, disfluency-removed, and disfluency-removed with stopword filtering) using k-interword, moving-window, and sentence-to-sentence comparisons, summarized with various statistical descriptors. Features were compared between SSD and healthy volunteers and examined for associations with dimensions of thought and language disturbance, including inefficiency, incoherence, and impaired expressivity. Results: SSD was predominantly associated with increased semantic similarity across models and comparison strategies. Model performance varied by preprocessing. RoBERTa performed best on minimally processed transcripts, yielding the greatest number of diagnosis-associated features, whereas GPT-2 achieved the largest diagnostic effect size after maximal preprocessing. GPT-2 showed the strongest signal for inefficiency and incoherence, while RoBERTa yielded the greatest number of associations with impaired expressivity. Conclusions: SSD diagnosis and its dimensions of thought and language abnormalities are characterized primarily by greater semantic proximity in open-ended speech. Optimal preprocessing depends on model architecture and the clinical dimension of interest, highlighting the importance of model- and phenotype-specific analytic choices in computational studies of thought and language disturbance in SSD.

items.title_en: Evidence-Based WASHmobile Anticipatory Action Framework to Reduce Cholera Outbreaks during Extreme Weather Events in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.title_zh: 基于证据的WASHmobile前瞻性行动框架以减少刚果民主共和国极端天气事件期间的霍乱暴发
items.abstract_en: Extreme weather contributes to cholera outbreaks globally. We examined associations between extreme weather and cholera through 4 years of surveillance at 115 healthcare facilities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and built an anticipatory action framework through WASHmobile for water, sanitation, and hygiene mobile messaging during extreme weather. Drought and wet conditions were defined using 3-month Standardized Precipitation Indices with CHIRPS data. A test-negative design assessed associations between extreme weather and culture-confirmed Vibrio cholerae among 1,068 diarrhea patients. Odds of cholera were higher during drought (OR: 1.94, 95% CI: 1.17-3.20) and extreme wet conditions (OR: 2.22, 95% CI: 1.39-3.55). During drought conditions in our randomized controlled trial of 2334 participants, handwashing with soap significantly declined in the standard arm but not the WASHmobile arm. Findings informed an anticipatory action framework where pre-defined climate triggers activate WASHmobile as an early warning system to reduce cholera outbreaks during extreme weather.

items.title_en: Receipt of guideline-concordant prenatal care among Medicaid-insured women with disabilities in Texas
items.title_zh: 德克萨斯州享受Medicaid保险的残疾女性接受符合指南的产前保健情况
items.abstract_en: Objective: To assess receipt of guideline-concordant prenatal care among pregnant women with disabilities enrolled in Medicaid. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 748,304 births to women enrolled in Texas Medicaid from 2010-2015. Births were classified into three groups by maternal disability status: no disability, receipt of federal disability benefits (STAR+), or disability identified through ICD-9 codes. Guideline-concordant care was defined as receipt of recommended prenatal services at recommended times. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for guideline-concordant care, adjusting for covariates. Results: There were 20,700 births (2.8%) to women with disabilities, 40.1% of whom were enrolled in STAR+. Fewer than half of women in any group received guideline-concordant testing for D(Rh) antigen, rubella, complete blood count, bacteriuria, or glucose tolerance. Women in STAR+ were more likely than those without disabilities to receive no prenatal care (9.4% vs. 1.6%), despite higher first-trimester initiation among those who accessed care. STAR+ enrollment was associated with substantially lower odds of guideline-concordant testing, including HIV (aOR 0.27; 95% CI, 0.26-0.29), syphilis (0.33; 0.31-0.35), hepatitis B (0.38; 0.36-0.40), D(Rh) antigen (0.31; 0.30-0.33), anatomy ultrasound (0.32; 0.31-0.34), and glucose (0.42; 0.40-0.44). Women with disabilities identified via ICD-9 codes also had lower odds, though differences were smaller. Conclusion for practice: Guideline-concordant prenatal care was suboptimal overall and especially deficient among women receiving federal disability benefits, underscoring the need for targeted quality improvement in Medicaid prenatal care delivery.

items.title_en: Maternal Vaginal Pathogenic Bacterial Colonization and Early-Onset Neonatal Sepsis in Mwanza City, Tanzania: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.title_zh: 坦桑尼亚姆万扎市母亲阴道致病性细菌定植与早发型新生儿败血症：一项前瞻性队列研究
items.abstract_en: Background: Early-onset neonatal sepsis (EONS) remains a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries. Maternal vaginal pathogenic bacterial colonization and HIV infection may increase the risk of EONS through vertical transmission and immune dysregulation, but prospective evidence from sub-Saharan Africa is limited. This study assessed the association between maternal HIV status, vaginal pathogenic bacterial colonization, and EONS among women delivering at five selected health facilities in Mwanza City, Tanzania. Methods: A prospective comparative cohort study was conducted between August 2023 and February 2025 among 580 pregnant women delivering at five selected health facilities in Mwanza City. A maternal lower vaginal swab was collected before delivery for bacterial culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Neonates were followed for seven days after birth to identify EONS using standardized clinical and laboratory criteria, with culture confirmation where applicable. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to estimate incidence rates and identify independent predictors of neonatal sepsis. Results: Overall, 89 neonates developed EONS, yielding a cumulative incidence of 15.3% and an incidence rate of 2.42 per 100 person-days (95% CI: 1.97-2.98). Twenty-four (27.0%) cases were culture-confirmed, while 65 (73.0%) were clinically diagnosed. Neonates born to colonized mothers had substantially higher sepsis incidence than those born to non-colonized mothers (3.41 vs. 0.34 per 100 person-days). After adjustment, maternal vaginal bacterial colonization was the strongest predictor of neonatal sepsis (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 9.52, 95% CI: 3.47-26.09; p<0.001). Maternal HIV infection independently increased the hazard of neonatal sepsis by 76% (aHR 1.76, 95% CI: 1.14-2.73; p=0.011), while maternal malaria doubled the risk (aHR 2.74, 95% CI: 1.43-5.22; p=0.002). Escherichia coli (E. coli) accounted for 58.3% of culture-confirmed neonatal infections, followed by both Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus (20.8% each). Conclusion: Maternal vaginal pathogenic bacterial colonization was strongly associated with early-onset neonatal sepsis. Maternal HIV infection and malaria were also independently associated with increased sepsis. The findings support strengthening maternal infection prevention, neonatal surveillance, and microbiological diagnostic capacity, while prospective intervention studies are needed to determine whether targeted screening and prevention of maternal bacterial colonization can reduce neonatal sepsis.

items.title_en: Clinical and prognostic significance of the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index in breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.title_zh: C反应蛋白-白蛋白-淋巴细胞（CALLY）指数在乳腺癌中的临床和预后意义：系统评价与荟萃分析
items.abstract_en: Background: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index integrates inflammatory, nutritional and immune-related biomarkers and may offer an accessible measure of host status in breast cancer. However, its prognostic relevance and clinical value remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated its associations with survival and treatment response and examined predictive performance. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, supplemented by reference-list and forward-citation searching. Studies evaluating CALLY in adults with invasive breast cancer were eligible. Multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) comparing low versus high baseline CALLY were pooled using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp intervals. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Results: Nine publications included 2,568 reported patients. Four studies comprising 1,394 patients contributed to each survival synthesis. Low CALLY yielded pooled HRs of 2.03 for overall survival (95% CI 1.20-3.45; I2=72.4%) and 2.00 for disease-free survival (95% CI 0.91-4.41; I2=77.7%). Both intervals included no association. In one HER2-positive cohort, low baseline CALLY was associated with lower odds of pathological complete response (adjusted OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.50). Apparent overall-survival area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) ranged from 0.688 to 0.740. External validation and demonstrated clinical utility were absent. Conclusions: CALLY shows potential prognostic and treatment-response associations, but imprecision, heterogeneity and limited validation prevent routine clinical adoption. Standardized measurement, prospective validation and demonstration of incremental clinical value are needed. Keywords: Breast cancer; C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index; Prognosis; Survival; Pathological complete response; Meta-analysis

items.title_en: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
items.title_zh: 纵向AI模型预测癌症不良事件
items.abstract_en: Clinical interventions for cancer treatment toxicities can reduce morbidity, mortality, and healthcare cost, if high risk patients can be identified. We developed SPARC, a transformer-based foundation model, using real-world, longitudinal, routinely collected health measurements, to predict adverse event risk. Pre-training and fine-tuning SPARC on 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients with cancer led to state-of-the-art performance at predicting cancer-related adverse events on (i) held-out data from the development cohort, (ii) a prospective validation cohort from the same center (Npatients=23,126), (iii) multiple publicly available external datasets (Npatients=26,012), and (iv) external, multi-hospital cohorts (Npatients=562,620, 206,840). SPARC generalized to multiple external centers and identified patients most likely to benefit from an intervention (G-CSF). Pooled multi-institution, more than single-institution, fine-tuning improved generalizability. We release SPARC as a community resource. Our results highlight the utility of AI time series models in oncologic management.

items.title_en: The genetic, clinical and immune landscape of clonal hematopoiesis across adulthood in the multi-ancestry Mount Sinai Million cohort
items.abstract_en: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), the age-associated expansion of blood cell clones carrying acquired driver mutations, remains less well characterized in young adults, across genetic ancestries, and in clinical populations. We analyzed whole-exome sequencing and longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from 59,598 adults in the Mount Sinai Million Health Discoveries Program, an urban, multi-ancestry hospital-based cohort that includes substantial representation of African ([~]35%) and Admixed American genetic ancestry ([~]15%) and young adults aged 18-39 years ([~]30%). After sample QC, separate analyses were performed in discovery (n = 28,051) and validation (n = 26,938) cohorts defined by sequencing platform and combined by meta-analysis. CHIP was detected in 8.5% of participants in each cohort and in 4.0% of young adults, with DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, and PPM1D the most frequently mutated genes. Prevalence and clone size increased with age across ancestry groups. After adjusting for age, participants of African ancestry had lower CHIP prevalence than those of European ancestry in both cohorts (discovery: OR=0.86, 95% CI = 0.78-0.95, p=0.002; validation: OR=0.84, 95% CI = 0.75-0.93, p=0.001). Participants of Admixed American ancestry showed a similar trend. Higher systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) was associated with CHIP after adjusting for age, sex and ancestry in both cohorts (pooled OR=1.30, 95% CI = 1.15-1.48, p=4.78e-5). Heterozygosity at an HLA class II locus HLA-DPA1 was associated with 7% lower odds of overall CHIP (pooled OR=0.93, 95% CI = 0.87-0.99, p=0.03). Driver-stratified analyses revealed distinct HLA class II nominal association patterns for DNMT3A- and TET2-mutant CHIP. Particularly, HLA-DQB1 heterozygosity associated with lower odds of TET2-mutant CHIP (pooled OR=0.84, 95% CI = 0.70-1.00, p=0.05), HLA-DQA1 and HLA-DOB heterozygosity associated with higher odds of DNMT3A-mutant CHIP (pooled OR=1.19, 95% CI = 1.00-1.42, p=0.05; pooled OR=1.12, 95% CI = 1.01-1.25, p=0.03 respectively). Longitudinal EHR analyses revealed CHIP associations with several incident diseases that varied by driver gene and clone size. The broadest pattern of associations involved high-risk CHIP genes and encompassed hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, cardiovascular outcomes, hypertension, and COPD. High-VAF clones were the main drivers of these associations. Among adults aged [≥] 40 years, phenome-wide analyses identified a Bonferroni-significant association with incident myeloproliferative disease and nominal associations with incident pancytopenia, anemia, cardiomegaly, and chronic renal failure. Young-adult CHIP was nominally associated with incident nodular goiter and esophageal disease. These findings characterize CHIP across adulthood and genetic ancestry and reveal inherited immune variation and systemic inflammation as correlates in a hospital-based population.

items.title_en: COVID-19 mortality in six Caribbean countries during Four Waves of the COVID-19 Pandemic
items.abstract_en: Background: Mortality associated with COVID-19 in the Caribbean during specific waves and exposure to different variants has not well described, especially for the six most populous English-speaking countries (Bahamas, Barbados, Guyana, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago, and St. Lucia), compared to the United Kingdom (UK). Methods: The first four waves of the pandemic, cases and deaths were estimated from epidemiologic curves on Johns Hopkins University Coronavirus Resource Center for the countries of interest from 10-Mar-20 to 12-Aug-22. Crude mortality rates (CMR), case fatality ratios (CFR) and standardized mortality ratios (SMR) were calculated using England as the standard population. Findings: The six countries reported 550,657 cases and 10,259 COVID-19 deaths. First wave Caribbean CFRs (1-3%) were significantly lower than the UK (20%). Thereafter (1-Apr-21 to 31-May-22) Caribbean SMRs exceeded 1 (range: 1.37-6.35) while UK CFRs declined to 2.3% (2nd wave) and 0.2% (3rd wave). Caribbean CFRs were highest with circulation of the Delta variant in the 2nd and 3rd waves. Barbados had the lowest SMR (0.65). COVID-19 vaccine roll-out (since Feb-Mar 2021) first targeted high-risk groups (elderly, health workers, co-morbidities). No Caribbean country achieved the global full vaccination target (70%) by the 4th wave, range: 21% (Jamaica) to 54% (Barbados), compared to 86% for the UK. Interpretation: Early in the COVID-19 pandemic, Caribbean CFRs were lower than the UK, probably due to more intensive non-pharmaceutical interventions. Limited vaccine coverage negatively impacted mortality in later waves, which was highest when the Delta variant was prevalent, declining with the later Omicron variant.

items.title_en: Multi-scale analysis of the HIF1A hypoxia-inflammation axis in severe COVID-19
items.abstract_en: Objective and design: To test whether the hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1A) axis links transcriptional, cellular, biomarker and host-genetic features of severe COVID-19, in a retrospective multi-scale observational study of public cohorts and one hospital cohort. Material or subjects: 35,268 hospitalized patients (Mexican national registry); 1,100 samples from five bulk RNA-seq cohorts; 25,773 peripheral neutrophils from six individuals; 326 hospitalized patients (Sao Paulo, Brazil); 93 hospitalized patients (University Clinical Center Kragujevac, Serbia). Treatment: None. Methods: Within-cohort effect sizes for a 10-gene HIF1A panel; single-cell pathway scoring; logistic regression and gradient boosting with SHAP; TaqMan genotyping of HIF1A rs11549465 and rs41508050; cross-validation with bootstrap confidence intervals. Results: HIF1A (mean Cohen d +0.39) and LDHA (+0.76) were higher in severe disease in all five cohorts. Neutrophils of all three patients who failed extubation scored higher than those of both weaned patients and over-expressed S100A8/A9. C-reactive protein dominated ICU prediction; laboratory variables raised the AUC from 0.636 to 0.794. In Kragujevac, a clinical model predicted severe outcome (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.75 to 0.92). rs11549465 CT/TT carriers had lower mortality (1/11 vs 28/78; p = 0.095). Conclusions: HIF1A pathway activation is reproducible across cohorts and localizes to an alarmin-rich neutrophil state; host-genetic effects require larger cohorts.

items.title_en: SPARK: Bayesian structure learning of enhancer-based gene regulatory networks from single-cell multiomics data and prior knowledge
items.title_zh: SPARK：基于单细胞多组学数据与先验知识的增强子基因调控网络贝叶斯结构学习
items.abstract_en: Enhancer-based gene regulatory networks (eGRNs) linking enhancers with recruited transcription factors (TFs) and downstream target genes can help decipher complex regulatory mechanisms, such as the function of GWAS variants at enhancers. Molecular assays that profile gene expression and chromatin state jointly from the same cells (such as 10x Multiome) are a rich source of input data for eGRN reconstruction. However, these assays lack mechanistic evidence for enhancer-gene and TF-enhancer links, which can be contributed by prior knowledge from other assays and analyses. Here, we present SPARK, an eGRN reconstruction framework that formally combines single-cell multiome data with mechanistic prior knowledge. SPARK represents eGRNs as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and learns them using Bayesian inference, with a prior on the network structure constructed from heterogeneous sources of evidence. In a simulation study, we show that SPARK benefits from prior knowledge and outperforms existing DAG-based and regression-based algorithms. Finally, we use SPARK to study the regulatory circuitry of enhancers harboring immune disease GWAS variants in human primary monocytes, revealing known and novel regulatory links as candidates for experimental validation.

items.title_en: Understanding the role of IQ motif-containing GTPase-activating protein 1 as a potential disruptor of the essential adhesion module at cell-cell junctions
items.title_zh: 理解含IQ基序的GTPase激活蛋白1作为细胞间连接关键黏附模块潜在破坏因子的作用
items.abstract_en: A key mechanism of stabilization of Cadherin-based cell-cell adhesions is through a mechanically modulated interaction to cortical actin filaments. This interaction is facilitated by a cytoplasmic adhesion module comprising of a complex of {beta}-catenin/-catenin. Recent evidence shows that under specific conditions the {beta}-catenin/-catenin complex gets disrupted because of mechanical disregulation of the junction maintenance machinery. The IQ motif-containing GTPase-activating protein 1 (IQGAP1) plays apparently a vital role as an internal regulator of the adhesion module, which competes for binding on {beta}-catenin with -catenin and is able to dissociate the latter from the adhesion complex. The underlying molecular mechanism is poorly understood with no clear evidence on what types of interactions are critical for a potential disruption. In this work, we combine steered-molecular-dynamics simulations and a multi-step protein-protein docking framework to dissect how mechanical detachment of -catenin from the adhesion complex modulates the interactions between IQGAP1 and {beta}-catenin. Our simulations show that as -catenin detaches from {beta}-catenin, IQGAP1 docks with progressively favorable scores. Interfacial analysis and subsequent mutagenesis studies, allow us to predict a molecular mechanism for an IQGAP1-driven disruption of the junctional adhesion module that centers on early onset of key favorable electrostatic interactions.

items.title_en: Structure constrained spin responses of an FMN superoxide radical-pair model in mitochondrial complex I
items.title_zh: 线粒体复合物I中FMN超氧自由基对模型的结构约束自旋响应
items.abstract_en: Mitochondrial complex I produces reactive oxygen species at its flavin mononucleotide (FMN) cofactor. We combined steric sampling of oxygen positions in human complex I with radical-pair spin simulations to examine how the FMN pocket shapes reaction-yield sensitivity, which provided singlet yields across FMN O2 centroid separations, magnetic fields and spin-dephasing conditions. A composite score combining geometric accessibility with normalised field and dephasing responses peaked near 3.3 in the reference 2.5 ~9.0 calculation. The highest-scoring 10% of accessible configurations had a mean separation of 3.28 (2.5th~97.5th percentiles, 2.77~3.64 ). The near contact score maximum persisted when the structural input, sampled distance range and recombination/dephasing rates were varied. At longer separations, the raw field response approached a broad plateau, while the composite score retained a near-contact maximum. Prescribed fluctuations in separation produced the greatest variability in calculated singlet yield within or close to this region. The analysis locates an FMN-centred range of accessible geometries where structural and spin-response effects combine in a model of radical-pair reaction branching.

items.title_en: pamiR: INVESTIGATING PLANT CELLS ONE ORGANELLE AT A TIME
items.title_zh: pamiR：逐个细胞器研究植物细胞
items.abstract_en: Plant cell biochemistry is highly compartmentalized. Hence, forward genetic screening in an organelle-specific manner holds great potential to reveal novel loci controlling cell physiology. However, conventional forward genetics is a) limited by functional redundancy that can mask phenotypes in plant gene families and b) lacks organelle specificity. Here, we present the plastid-focused artificial microRNA (pamiR) resource designed to silence individual nuclear genes or co-targetable gene-family subsets encoding the organelle's proteome. The library contains 2,285 artificial microRNAs directed against 2,202 genes selected from a plastid-enriched, proteomics-supported target set. The constructs are expressed by a constitutive UBQ10 promoter in a binary vector carrying the FAST seed-fluorescence marker, allowing transformant selection before germination. Two proof-of-concept screens, one using photosynthetic phenotyping and one using paclobutrazol, a gibberellin biosynthesis inhibitor, recovered lines with phenotypes previously associated with simultaneous perturbation of multiple members of redundant plastid gene families such as light-harvesting complex b1 (LHCB1), K+ efflux antiporter (KEA), and 9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase (NCED). We experimentally confirmed specific target depletion for selected candidates, including paralogue-resolved LHCB1 depletion by mass spectrometry, and provide predicted off-target annotations for all 2,285 guides. Untargeted LHCB family members remained unchanged, and across the proteins included in the proteome-wide differential-abundance analysis, no additional significantly decreased protein was detected. KEA1 immunoreactive signal also fell below the immunoblot detection limit in pamiRkea1/2 and an independent KEA1/KEA2 amiRNA line. Together, these data establish pamiR as a plastid-specific screening resource and provide a framework for prioritizing and independently validating candidate phenotypes.

items.title_en: Memory-based and surround-based pattern completion show distinct laminar profiles in human V1
items.title_zh: 基于记忆与基于周围的模式补全在人类V1中表现出不同的层状分布
items.abstract_en: Visual input is often incomplete, requiring the brain to infer missing information from prior experience or contextual cues. Establishing whether memory-derived and context-derived information shape pattern completion through shared or distinct top-down pathways is central to understanding how perception emerges from the integration of sensory input and prior knowledge. Across two experiments, we used 7T layer fMRI to measure activity in an occluded region of human V1 while participants viewed natural scenes. Memory-based completion was enabled by varying the level of exposure to full scene images before scanning, while surround-based completion was implemented via two scenes that were repeatedly presented in partially occluded form but never seen intact. In both fMRI experiments, category decoding in the occluded V1 region only emerged after multiple prior exposures, whereas novel scenes did not show reliable decoding. Repeated partially occluded scenes also supported decoding, despite the hidden region never being shown, consistent with surround-based pattern completion. Critically, mnemonic and surround-based pattern completion showed opposite laminar decoding profiles across V1 depths, with mnemonic feedback dominating deep layers, and surround-based feedback dominating superficial layers. Together, these findings suggest that completion in the early visual cortex depends on the sources of inferred information, revealing dissociable feedback pathways for memory- and context-driven inference.

items.title_en: Inferring brain structural complexity from dynamical measures
items.title_zh: 从动力学指标推断脑结构复杂性
items.abstract_en: Complexity, commonly defined as the coexistence of integration and differentiation, is a fundamental property of thalamocortical networks and is regarded as a prerequisite for adaptive brain function and consciousness. A variety of metrics have been developed to estimate neural complexity from recorded activity and are increasingly employed in both research and clinical settings. Yet, the extent to which these measures reflect specific architectural features of the underlying circuits remains poorly understood. Here, we used Wilson-Cowan mean-field equations to simulate neural dynamics across networks spanning a broad range of architectures. By systematically rewiring connectivity, we generated graded variations in the structural integration-differentiation balance and assessed a panel of complexity measures derived either from spontaneous activity (observational metrics) or from responses to external perturbations (perturbational metrics). Observational measures exhibited markedly heterogeneous behavior: some were primarily sensitive to network integration, others to differentiation, whereas some showed limited sensitivity to architectural manipulations. In contrast, perturbational measures robustly peaked at intermediate rewiring steps and scaled with small-worldness, consistent with architectures that combine local recurrence and distributed communication. Moreover, perturbational metrics proved robust to common-driver confounds and were highest in a wake-like regime near critical instability, declining as sleep-like dynamics became more widespread across the network. Taken together, these findings map widely used empirical complexity measures onto specific network architectures, reveal dynamical factors that can bias observational estimates, and provide guidance for inferring complexity in systems whose internal organization is inaccessible, unconventional, or only partially known, including brain organoids, non-human nervous systems, and synthetic neural networks.

items.title_en: Similarity in greater Chinese ideology is associated with intersubject neural similarity during viewing of a pro-China video
items.title_zh: 大中华意识形态相似性与观看亲华视频时的受试者间神经相似性相关
items.abstract_en: When people watch the same political narrative, they often form different interpretations. Although prior research has shown that political ideology can shape shared neural responses to sociopolitical content, less is known about how individual differences in national identity ideology are associated with inter-individual similarity in neural dynamics during naturalistic viewing, particularly in sociopolitical contexts where national identity is highly salient in public discourse. We examined Greater Chinese ideology, one dimension of national identity ideology, in relation to positive engagement and neural dynamics during viewing of the same pro-China video across two samples in Taiwan. In Study 1 (N = 52), higher Greater Chinese ideology was associated with greater positive engagement. In Study 2 (N = 60), participants underwent fMRI while viewing the same video. Intersubject representational similarity analysis showed that greater similarity in participants' Greater Chinese ideology item-response profiles was associated with greater similarity in neural dynamics in regions associated with the frontoparietal control, salience, and default mode networks. Notably, the within-versus-between neural similarity effect was stronger among participants with relatively lower Greater Chinese ideology scores than among those with relatively higher scores. These findings link Greater Chinese ideology to positive engagement and similarity in neural dynamics during viewing of this pro-China video. Further research is needed to determine whether similar associations can be observed across other dimensions of national identity ideology and different political narratives.

items.title_en: Estimating the Direct Impact of Influenza Vaccination and Vaccine-Averted Illnesses Using an Extended Static Compartmental Model
items.title_zh: 使用扩展静态房室模型估计流感疫苗接种及疫苗所避免疾病的直接影响
items.abstract_en: A previously developed static compartment model informed influenza program decisions by estimating the direct impact of influenza vaccination. To improve the estimation of the burden averted by vaccination, we extended this model to consider multiple influenza seasons, allow natural and vaccine-induced immunity to wane over time allow influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) to differ by hospitalized versus non-hospitalized influenza-associated illness, and measure deaths averted. For model demonstration, we created a synthetic Northern Hemisphere-like and year-round influenza activity dataset spanning four seasons among older adults (>65 years) and assumed VE against symptomatic illness of 37% (17%-53%) and VE against hospitalization of 45% (28%-59%). Under Northern Hemisphere-like activity and an existing vaccination program with an average annual vaccine coverage of 33%, vaccination averted 15.1% (95% UI: 12.2%-16.3%) of influenza-associated illnesses across four seasons; the annual prevented fraction for hospitalized deaths ranged from 14.4% (95% UI: 11.7%-16.8%) to 18.5% (95% UI: 14.9%-21.5%). Under a hypothetical year-round vaccination program with an annual coverage of 20%, vaccination averted 4.9% (95% UI: 3.8%-5.4%) of influenza-associated illnesses across four seasons; the annual prevented fraction for hospitalized deaths ranged from 5.5% (95% UI: 4.3%-6.5%) and 5.8% (95% UI: 4.8%-6.6%). These model extensions allow estimation of vaccine-averted burden across multiple seasons and diverse vaccination program settings, providing information to support influenza vaccination decision-making.

items.title_en: Modelled mortality benefits of reducing fibrinolysis resistance in sepsis: integrating observational and ex vivo data
items.title_zh: 降低脓毒症纤溶抵抗的建模死亡率获益：整合观察性与离体数据
items.abstract_en: Background. Suppressed fibrinolysis (fibrinolysis resistance) is increasingly recognised as a driver of organ failure in sepsis, yet trials in sepsis-induced coagulopathy have largely targeted coagulation rather than fibrinolysis. This study combined an observational ICU cohort with nested analyses of plasma fibrinolysis proteins and ex vivo reversibility, modelling the potential mortality reduction from restoring fibrinolytic capacity to inform trial design. Methods. In 188 adults admitted to ICU with sepsis, repeated tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)-enhanced viscoelastometric testing quantified fibrinolysis resistance as the fibrin adjusted lysis time (TPA-LT/FIBA10) and as ordinal Grades 1-3 of worsening resistance. Adjusted logistic regression and time-varying Cox models related fibrinolysis resistance to death within 28 days of admission, with unmeasured confounding assessed by E-values. In nested sub-studies, plasma fibrinolysis proteins were measured and whole blood was tested ex vivo for reversal of resistance by supplemental tPA, plasminogen, or an inhibitory antibody to a2-antiplasmin (a2AP iAb). Ex vivo effects were modelled onto the observed fibrinolysis resistance-mortality relationship using a hypothetical intervention distribution framework. Results. Each e-fold (~2.72) increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10 was associated with a 2.2-fold (95% CI 1.5-3.3) increase in the odds of death in the fully adjusted logistic model and a 2.3-fold (1.6-3.2) increased hazard in the time-varying Cox model. Comparing the least (Grade 1) with the worst (Grade 3) resistance state, the odds ratio was 7.4 (2.4-23) and the hazard ratio 6.7 (3.0-15). Associations were robust to unmeasured confounding, with E-values of 3-13. Grade 3 resistance showed the highest PAI-1/tPA and a2AP/plasminogen ratios. Ex vivo supplementation with plasminogen or a2AP iAb reversed fibrinolysis resistance from Grade 3 to Grade 1. Modelling these effects yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of 18-21% across Grades 2 and 3, and 32-36% in Grade 3. Conclusions. Fibrinolysis resistance measured at the bedside in sepsis reflects mechanistically reversible changes in fibrinolytic balance ex vivo. Modelling reversal by plasminogen supplementation or a2AP inhibition yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of up to 32% in the most severe resistance state. These hypothesis-generating estimates identify candidate interventions and provide a rationale for a clinical trial.

items.title_en: Prevalence and determinants of problematic khat use in Ethiopia
items.title_zh: 埃塞俄比亚问题性卡塔使用的患病率与决定因素
items.abstract_en: **Background** Evidence on khat use prevalence is substantial in Ethiopia and elsewhere. However, problematic khat use remains largely understudied because the concept has not been clearly defined or consistently measured. This study estimated the prevalence and determinants of problematic khat use among Ethiopian adults. **Methods** This descriptive cross-sectional analysis used baseline data from a prospective khat cohort study conducted in Butajira and adjacent districts in Central Ethiopia Regional State. We included 504 khat users who had chewed khat within the previous five years. Problematic khat use was assessed using the locally developed and validated 17-item Problematic Khat Use Screening Tool (PKUST-17). A score of >17 indicated problematic use. Binary and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors. **Results** Among the 504 khat users, most were male (82.3%), married (85.0%), and rural residents (70.8%). The prevalence of problematic khat use was 19.6%. Daily or near-daily khat users had eightfold higher odds of problematic use than occasional users (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI: 3.75-17.24). Stressful life events were associated with 3.48-fold higher odds of problematic use (AOR = 3.48, 95% CI: 1.56-7.76), while depressive symptoms were associated with 3.70-fold higher odds (AOR = 3.70, 95% CI: 2.00-6.75). **Conclusion** Problematic khat use affects approximately one in five khat users in Ethiopia. It is strongly associated with frequent khat use, stressful life events, and depressive symptoms. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways and evaluate culturally appropriate prevention and treatment interventions.

items.title_en: Understanding widening socio-economic inequities in cardiovascular disease mortality in the Netherlands: A mixed methods protocol
items.abstract_en: Background: In the Netherlands, there is a substantial social gradient in mortality: individuals with higher socio-economic status are more likely to live longer lives than those with lower socio-economic status. There is evidence that this social gradient has widened since the mid-twentieth century, although why this has occurred is poorly understood. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) provides a particularly useful case study for understanding the mechanisms underlying this widening gradient. While CVD was historically the leading cause of death in the Netherlands, improvements in prevention and treatment have decreased CVD mortality, even as socio-economic inequalities in CVD mortality have increased. In this project, I aim to identify and test the mechanisms driving widening socio-economic inequities in CVD mortality over the last 75 years. Methods and analysis: This project uses mixed-methods. First, in participatory workshops, key stakeholders, e.g. policymakers, healthcare professionals, patient representatives, and individuals with lived experience of poverty, will co-create a conceptual model outlining the explanations linking socio-economic status and CVD in the Netherlands. Second, the conceptual model will provide the structure for the microsimulation, with the former defining which mechanisms will be represented in the latter. The microsimulation will maintain a common model structure across time, although population characteristics and individual trajectories will change to reflect successive twenty-year periods from the 1950s until today. The microsimulation will be validated by comparing simulated outcomes with historical data. Counterfactual scenarios will then be used to estimate the relative contribution of different mechanisms to the widening of socio-economic inequalities in CVD mortality. Ethics and dissemination: This project has been approved by the Social Sciences Research Ethics Committee of Wageningen University (approval number 2026-203). Participants will provide informed consent prior to participation. The microsimulation code will be made openly available, and findings will be disseminated through open-access publications, conference presentations, and a public summary co-designed with stakeholders.

items.title_en: MAScINSIGHT: A Real-World Data Study to Deepen Knowledge and Management of McCune-Albright Syndrome - Study Protocol for an Observational Study within OHDSI
items.abstract_en: Introduction McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is a rare congenital disorder affecting endocrine, skeletal and dermatological systems. MAS is often coded as fibrous dysplasia (FD) in routine health data, which includes other conditions and does not allow precise identification. This coding gap complicates reliable epidemiological estimates and clinical characterization. The study MAScINSIGHT aims to address this by investigating MAS features within FD-coded cohorts. Methods and analysis MAScINSIGHT is a retrospective observational study using a federated network of data in the OMOP Common Data Model. Routine data from multiple sites will be analyzed within a federated setting to assess endocrine abnormalities and treatment patterns in patients with FD or MAS. Ethics and dissemination Analyses will be performed locally at the data partner, with only aggregate statistics made available and centrally analyzed. The study protocol was approved by the ethics committee (reference number: 2026-18760-retrospektiv). Findings will be disseminated through open-access publications and patient-oriented reports.

items.title_en: Maternal Autoantibody Combinations as Predictors of Autism Risk: Retrospective Discovery and External Validation in a Prospective Cohort at Increased Risk
items.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Maternal Autoantibody-Related Autism (MARA) is a recently defined subset of autism characterized by specific combinations of maternal autoantibodies which cross the placenta and bind neurodevelopmentally critical target proteins. A clinical multi-ELISA MARA assay was recently rigorously analytically validated. The primary objective of this study was to assess the potential performance of this MARA autoantibody assay for predicting autism risk in high-risk populations. Secondary objectives were to establish the significant MARA autoantibody combinations and verify clinical discrimination in an external cohort. Methods: Bio-banked plasma samples from mothers of 420 autism and 335 typically developing (TD) children were analyzed by ELISA for MARA autoantibodies in combination. Transcendent autoantibody pairwise combinations were identified in discovery where both autoantibodies in a combination exceeded the values of every control participant. Permutation testing was used to establish that the probability of observed results significantly exceeded chance. Performance was then validated in an independent cohort (mothers of 42 autistic and 90 TD children). Results: Transcendent antibody levels were discovered in 70 mothers (16.7% of autism cases; no typically developing participants) in the discovery cohort. Specificity and positive predictive values for autism were 100% by construct. An external cohort showed similar performance with 14 (33.3%) transcendents. Permutation testing of each cohort demonstrated probabilities of transcendent cases to be significantly higher than expected be chance. Conclusions: The data reported here provides evidence for a high-risk subset of mothers of children with autism identified by the MARA autoantibody assay which enables further clinical validation.

items.title_en: A lifecourse perspective on sociodemographic intersectional inequalities in physical and mental health outcomes
items.abstract_en: Persistent inequalities in health outcomes continue to be a stubborn feature of many developed Western societies. To effectively understand health inequalities researchers must address two key criticisms: an overt focus on singular dimensions of disadvantage and a continuing need for longitudinal studies. Lifecourse intersectionality offers a framework to address these critiques through situating more nuanced and multidimensional understandings of the development of inequalities over time. We conduct a longitudinal Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) examining both physical and mental health SF12 scores using UK Household Longitudinal Study data for adults (2009 to 2023). Forming intersections based on sex, ethnicity, generational cohort, education, and socioeconomic class, we identify a substantial degree of intersectional variation in our outcomes, and distinct differences in the development of intersectional inequalities in physical and mental health over the lifecourse. Intersectional inequalities are more pronounced for mental health compared to physical health, particularly at younger and older ages. In both cases, inequalities are additively patterned with generation and sex appearing most important to mental health and socioeconomic differences being stronger for physical health. However, our results also emphasise heterogeneity in the identified lifecourse intersectional effects, particularly in relation to how the patterning of the sociodemographic components for mental health vary by generational cohort. We therefore help reveal important complexity in the development of health inequalities in the UK and highlight the utility of longitudinal intersectional MAIHDA as a tool for quantitative intersectional researchers.

items.title_en: Motion-robust high-resolution 3D-GRASE pseudo-continuous ASL perfusion imaging at 3T
items.abstract_en: Purpose: High resolution arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based perfusion imaging is desirable for many applications but suffers from low SNR and motion sensitivity due to the necessity for highly segmented readouts. Acquisition and reconstruction strategies were optimized for motion-robust high-resolution pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) of the brain at 3T using segmented 3D Gradient and Spin Echo (3D-GRASE) at 2.0-mm isotropic resolution. Methods: A high-resolution 3D-GRASE pCASL sequence was implemented at 3T and evaluated with a focus on the interaction between background suppression strength and motion-corrected reconstruction, together with the fat suppression and control-tag subtraction strategies that strong suppression requires. Motion correction was performed using a novel motion-compensated (alignedSENSE-based) reconstruction that simultaneously estimates the motion and image, accounting for contrast changes between tag and control data. Eight healthy volunteers were scanned under motion-free and cued motion conditions. Image quality was assessed against motion-free reference images using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Results: The optimized acquisition-reconstruction pipeline enabled robust 2.0-mm isotropic pCASL at 3T and showed improved resistance to motion-related degradation. Strong BGS provided near-complete suppression of static tissue, and water excitation reduced lipid contamination and improved coil sensitivity estimation. The regularized alignedSENSE motion correction further improved perfusion-image quality, increasing SSIM by 18.7% under Strong BGS. Conclusion: Robust high-resolution pCASL at 3T can be achieved through combined optimization of acquisition and reconstruction. The combination of Strong BGS, water excitation, reference-superimposed processing, and regularized motion correction mitigates motion-related degradation and yields higher-quality perfusion images for high-resolution ASL.

items.title_en: Comparative efficacy and safety of targeted disease-modifying therapies in adults with primary IgA nephropathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
items.abstract_en: Background: Targeted disease-modifying therapies for adults with primary IgA nephropathy are increasing in number. However, head-to-head evidence is limited, and trial endpoints and follow-up durations vary. The relative effects of these therapies on short-term proteinuria control, long-term kidney outcomes, and safety remain unclear. Methods: We searched databases and trial registries for randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with a planned treatment duration of at least 24 weeks alongside stable or optimized supportive care. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses evaluated baseline-adjusted geometric mean ratios (GMRs) for 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 32 to 40 and 24 to 52 weeks, with Holm correction applied. Total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope and composite kidney outcomes were synthesized using common-effect models. Serious adverse events (SAEs) were analyzed using penalized-likelihood logistic regression within risk windows. Sensitivity analyses included restriction to evidence at low risk of bias, exclusion of interim or stage-specific reports, and assessment of precision-recovery assumptions and time-window boundaries. The Mantel to Haenszel method without continuity correction assessed the robustness of sparse SAE results. RoB 2 and CINeMA assessed risk of bias and evidence certainty, respectively. Results: Seventeen trials were included. At 32 to 40 weeks, telitacicept and subcutaneous sibeprenlimab had the lowest GMR point estimates versus placebo: 0.450 (nominal 95% CI 0.323 to 0.628) and 0.488 (0.355 to 0.671), respectively. None of the seven targeted treatment comparisons reached statistical significance after Holm correction. Iptacopan had the largest point estimate for improvement in annualized total eGFR slope: 3.020 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI 2.025 to 4.015). Composite kidney outcome hazard ratios were 0.570 (95% CI 0.401 to 0.811) for iptacopan and 0.440 (0.271 to 0.714) for targeted-release budesonide. Telitacicept had the lowest SAE odds ratio point estimate at 36 to 39 weeks: 0.314 (95% CI 0.105 to 0.938), although safety estimates were imprecise. In sensitivity analyses, proteinuria effect directions were generally consistent, but the 95% CIs for all retained comparisons included 1 after excluding interim or stage-specific reports; sparse SAE estimates remained imprecise. Evidence certainty was rated as low or very low. Conclusion: Although some regimens yielded the most favorable point estimates, the available evidence remains insufficient to establish treatment priorities or comparative safety advantages. Head-to-head trials are needed.

items.title_en: Distinct neural representations encode psychiatric states across timescales
items.abstract_en: Psychiatric states manifest over multiple timescales, from transient fluctuations in disorder-related distress to long-term variations in disease severity, yet whether these expressions share common neural representations remains unknown. We addressed this question in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) by comparing neural activity associated with momentary distress evoked by triggers versus that associated with clinically assessed chronic symptom severity. We analyzed intracranial recordings from the ventral capsule and orbitofrontal cortex spanning more than 4595 patient-days in 8 individuals undergoing deep brain stimulation therapy (NCT03457675, NCT04281134, NCT04806516), together with quantitative facial- and speech-derived behavioral measures. Neural signatures of OCD severity were dissociable from and stronger than signatures of momentary distress, indicating distinct underlying brain states. Integrating behavioral data into a predictive computational model improved neural decoding performance of both momentary distress and OCD severity. These findings show that acute manifestations of psychiatric illness are not simply short-timescale readouts of the same neural states that encode longer-term clinical burden. Instead, transient distress and longitudinal disease severity are represented by dissociable neural processes. This distinction has important implications for how psychiatric biomarkers and adaptive neuromodulation strategies should be designed.

items.title_en: Beyond reduced alpha power: a weaker temporal link between alpha and other brain rhythms in Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract_en: Background: Reduced alpha power is among the most consistently reported resting electroencephalography (EEG) features of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, alpha activity also interacts with other rhythms over time, a dynamic aspect that power measures do not capture. Whether AD weakens this temporal interaction, and whether such a change carries information beyond reduced alpha power, remains unclear. Methods: We analyzed public eyes-closed resting EEG from 29 healthy controls (HC), 36 patients with AD and 23 with frontotemporal dementia (FTD). After separating periodic from aperiodic activity, we tracked the aperiodic exponent and periodic theta, alpha, beta and gamma activity in consecutive 1-s windows. A vector autoregressive model predicted these five measures from the preceding window. Alpha's predictive contribution (G) was the increase in prediction error for theta, beta and gamma when the model was refitted without alpha as a predictor, with training and testing on separate time blocks of each recording. AD-HC differences were adjusted for age and sex, then for alpha expression (periodic alpha power) and signal quality (dynamic range and spatial reliability), with alpha self-persistence (alpha's carry-over between windows) as a benchmark. We also tested whether expression and G each added information about AD beyond the other. An exploratory Jansen-Rit-family circuit model examined whether expression and G can change partly independently. Results: G was lower in AD than in HC (adjusted difference in 10^3G, -3.19; 95% confidence interval -5.25 to -1.13; p = 0.0035), with a consistent direction across sensitivity analyses. Adjustment for alpha expression and signal quality retained 75.8% of this difference but only 4.4% of the self-persistence difference. Expression and G each added information beyond the other (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012 for both). FTD contrasts were inconclusive. In the circuit model, reducing local recurrent excitation lowered alpha expression without an estimated decrease in G, whereas reducing downstream input lowered G with a smaller change in expression. Conclusions: At the group level, the resting alpha abnormality in AD comprises two partly nonredundant dimensions: reduced expression and a weaker temporal link between alpha and subsequent multi-rhythm activity. Quantifying this temporal link may complement conventional spectral markers of AD.

items.title_en: A family-aware All of Us benchmark for polygenic prediction and genomic machine learning
items.abstract_en: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have improved substantially in predictive performance, yet results remain difficult to compare across studies that differ in cohorts, phenotype definitions, and evaluation procedures. Comparison to machine-learning methods is harder still, since their performance depends strongly on how data are partitioned and whether related individuals leak across splits. Here, we introduce a family-aware benchmark for polygenic prediction built on version 9 of the All of Us Research Program (AoU). The benchmark assigns entire family components to fixed discovery, calibration, and test partitions, reserves first-degree relatives for within-family evaluation, and separates models trained only on AoU discovery data from those using external GWAS summary statistics. This enables direct comparison between conventional PRS pipelines and machine-learning models trained under identical data budgets. We report results for 14 binary disease traits. Our strongest scores explain 5.7-24.9% of liability-scale variance, with particularly strong prediction for Alzheimer's disease, type 2 diabetes, prostate cancer, glaucoma, and inflammatory bowel disease, and match or exceed published commercial and academic scores for most traits. Across 12 traits with interpretable within-family estimates of within-sibship-to-population effect ratio, 11 confidence intervals included a ratio of 1. Type 2 diabetes showed an attenuation ratio of 0.86 [0.76, 0.97].

items.title_en: Predicting Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Treatment Outcomes: A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Topological Data Analysis Augmentation
items.abstract_en: We asked what topological structure adds to a clinical prediction model and how that addition should be measured. Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment outcome prediction is the testbed. The contribution is an evaluation design and a bounded null result. Cross-sectional records for 9210 patients from the NIAID TB Portals programme were collated to one row per patient by worst-case aggregation, giving a 99-feature clinical schema. We derived two topological representations. A Mapper graph, built on a UMAP lens over a Gower dissimilarity, supplied four neighbourhood-position features. Local Vietoris--Rips persistent homology on each patient's 26-point neighbourhood supplied degree-0 and degree-1 summaries, vectorised by the best of thirteen catalogued methods. We compared five feature configurations across four classifiers in a pipeline in which every topological step is fitted inside the training partition. A sealed test lockbox of 1776 patients, 463 of them with adverse outcomes, was opened once. We compared discrimination by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) using paired DeLong tests with Bonferroni correction (corrected threshold 0.0125). No topologically augmented configuration meaningfully improved lockbox AUROC over the clinical-only baseline under any classifier. The best AUROC was 0.7548, achieved by the baseline with XGBoost. Across all sixteen comparisons the upper 95% confidence limit never exceeded +0.014 AUROC. Five comparisons met the corrected threshold. Four favoured the baseline, and one, under the support vector machine, favoured the augmented model by a negligible +0.0005 AUROC.The same features supported neighbourhood-based risk stratification and revealed variation in adverse-outcome composition across patient neighbourhoods: adverse-outcome purity ranged from 5.9% to 30.5% across the fifteen largest Mapper nodes, stably under resampling. The findings support a complementary framing of topological data analysis in clinical prediction. Topological features are best understood not as replacements for clinical predictors but as an analytical lens that reveals geometric structure in the patient population not captured by the clinical feature representation alone.

items.title_en: Fibrinolysis resistance in sepsis assessed by serial beside viscoelastometry is associated with plasma protein profiles and organ-failure severity: a prospective observational study
items.abstract_en: Background: Fibrinolysis resistance is associated with adverse outcomes in sepsis and can be quantified at the bedside by tissue plasminogen activator-enhanced viscoelastometric testing, using the fibrin-adjusted (FIBA10) clot lysis time (TPA-LT) expressed as the TPA-LT/FIBA10 ratio. In this study of adults admitted to intensive care with sepsis, plasma tissue plasminogen activator activity, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 activity (PAI-1), plasminogen and a2-antiplasmin were measured serially alongside TPA-LT/FIBA10 and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA-2) scores. Whether the bedside TPA-LT/FIBA10 measure of fibrinolysis resistance reflects the underlying plasma fibrinolytic protein environment, and whether it tracks organ-failure severity, has not been established. Results: This prospective observational study included 283 paired observations in 69 septic patients admitted with a median Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation III score 81, median SOFA-2 score 13 and a 38% ICU mortality. PAI-1 increased and plasminogen decreased with increasing fibrinolysis resistance (1.77 [1.50-2.09]-fold increase and 0.81 [0.76-0.87]-fold decrease, respectively, per e-fold increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10). Increasing organ-failure severity was also associated with increased PAI-1 and decreased plasminogen (1.23 [1.17-1.29]-fold increase and 0.95 [0.93-0.96]-fold decrease, respectively, per point increase in SOFA-2). In contrast, tissue plasminogen activator activity and absolute a2-antiplasmin did not relate to fibrinolysis resistance or organ failure. Principal component analysis of the fibrinolysis proteins, organ-failure severity and fibrinolysis resistance identified a dominant axis explaining 35% of the variance, on which PAI-1, SOFA-2 and TPA-LT/FIBA10 loaded together in opposition to plasminogen. Unsupervised clustering of the dataset, performed without reference to patient outcomes, separated a fibrinolysis inhibitor- high, substrate-depleted group with 61% mortality compared to 29% in the preserved- fibrinolysis group. During the ICU stay, PAI-1 decreased within 72 hours in survivors but remained unchanged in non-survivors (interaction p<0.001). A trend was observed for plasminogen levels increasing in survivors but remaining static in non-survivors. Conclusions: Changes in key fibrinolysis proteins, organ-failure severity and fibrinolysis resistance measured by viscoelastometry were coupled facets of the response to sepsis dominated by fibrinolysis inhibitor excess and substrate depletion rather than by reduced activator availability. These findings provide biological validation for bedside viscoelastometric quantification of fibrinolysis resistance and support prospective evaluation of substrate-directed profibrinolytic strategies.

items.title_en: Interventions for Cognitive Impairment in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Umbrella Review of Pharmacological and Lifestyle Strategies, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications
items.abstract_en: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the fastest-growing epidemics associated with cognitive impairment and dementia. This reduces quality of life among patients with diabetes. Several trials on the management of cognitive impairment have been conducted, although their effectiveness and mechanisms are still unclear. Aim: To synthesize evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs examining interventions for cognitive impairment in T2DM, stratified by intervention category, comparator, patient characteristics, mechanisms, and clinical outcomes. Methods: We identified 11 systematic reviews (n = 213,604 participants) reporting the effects of cognitive impairment interventions through a comprehensive literature search. Using random-effects models, a meta-meta-analysis was conducted and heterogeneity assessed using I{superscript 2} statistics. AMSTAR and GRADE were used to assess the quality of reviews. Subgroup analyses were conducted for intervention category, cognitive severity, age, diabetes duration, sex, and follow-up duration. Results: Sodium glucose co-transporter inhibitors showed the strongest cognitive improvement effect (pooled OR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.35-0.55; SUCRA = 94.5%), followed by GLP-1 receptor agonists (RR/OR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.50-0.72; SUCRA = 92.1%). Among lifestyle interventions, multi-component exercise was the most effective (SMD = 0.69-1.04). The lower baseline cognition (MMSE < 23) benefited more from GLP-1 receptor agonists (Cohen's d = -3.00, p < 0.001). Advanced age ([≥]60 years) and prolonged intervention time ([≥]24 weeks for medications; [≥]6 months for exercise) were associated with greater effects. Female gender showed greater benefit from GLP-1 receptor agonists (HR = 0.63 vs 0.81 for male gender). Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists have the greatest effect on cognition in T2DM, and multi-component exercise is the most effective lifestyle component. The review therefore recommends individualized selection of interventions based on patient characteristics and baseline cognitive status. This calls for high-quality trials with prolonged follow-up to strengthen the evidence base.

items.title_en: Association between Blood Lead Levels and Anaemia in a Pregnant Population in the Kintampo Area of Ghana: A Prospective Cohort Study
items.abstract_en: Background: Maternal anaemia and lead exposure both pose substantial risks in pregnancy, but their relationship has not been consistently explored. We assessed trimester-specific blood lead levels (BLLs) and their association with anaemia in pregnant women in the Kintampo area of Ghana. Methods: In this prospective cohort study nested within the PRISMA Maternal and Newborn Health Study in Ghana, 300 pregnant women were enrolled at <14 weeks' gestation and followed until delivery. Trimester-specific venous blood was collected and analysed for haemoglobin levels using Sysmex XN 330 auto analyser (Sysmex Corporation, Japan) and BLL using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Anaemia was defined as 11.0g/dL for first (T1) and third (T3) trimesters and 10.5g/dL for second (T2) trimester according to the World Health Organisation's (WHO's) trimester-specific haemoglobin thresholds and elevated BLL as [≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Multiple logistic regression, adjusted for maternal age, parity, education, malaria parasitaemia, body mass index, gestational age and occupation, examined the BLL and anaemia association. A population-averaged Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) model was used to assess the association between elevated BLL and anaemia across trimesters. Results: The mean age of participants was 27.7{+/-}5.8 years (range 18-44years). Geometric mean BLL increased significantly across trimesters from 1.0 to 1.3 to 1.5 {micro}g/dL (p=0.003) for T1, T2 and T3 respectively. The prevalence of elevated BLL ([≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL) was 10.7%, 7.6%, and 15.2% for T1, T2, and T3 respectively. Anaemia prevalence increased significantly with increasing trimester from 34.7.0% to 59.3% to 76.0% (p<0.001) for T1, T2 and T3 respectively. In the population-averaged GEE model, elevated BLL was associated with increased odds of anaemia across trimesters, though this did not reach statistical significance (OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 0.77-2.17, p = 0.327). Conclusion: Anaemia prevalence in pregnancy is high in the Kintampo area and increases with advancing gestation. No significant association was observed between BLL and anaemia. These findings reinforce anaemia as a priority for urgent interventions in pregnancy through pathways independent of lead exposure. However, occupational lead surveillance and control remain important policy considerations.

items.title_en: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.abstract_en: Single-cell perturbation screens are used to train and evaluate models that predict perturbation effects, and model scores are judged against how reproducible the measured effects are. Reproducibility is usually judged by splitting each perturbation's cells into two random halves. This assumes that the halves are independent replicates. In pooled screens such as Perturb-seq, however, the cells carrying a guide RNA descend from a limited number of transduced cells, so two random halves contain the same clones: pseudoreplication whose unit is not marked in the data. Using perturbations that should have no effect as controls, we compared random halves with independent replicates from separate transductions, and tested directly with halves that differ only in their clones. In a genome-scale screen of primary T cells, null perturbations agreed between random halves almost always and between independent replicates only half the time, the rate expected from noise alone; measuring more cells did not remove this agreement. Splitting the cells into halves that share no clone, by the T-cell receptor constant region or by a clone barcode, largely removed the excess agreement. Its size equals the share of expression differences set by clones divided by the effective number of clones per perturbation; across 16 screens it was largest in T cells transferred into mice and in a genome-scale primary T-cell screen, one to two orders of magnitude smaller in cell lines, and smallest in non-dividing neurons. Shared clones inflate benchmark ceilings and reliability labels, and when a model's input and its scoring answer come from one transduction, published models that predict perturbation effects in a new cell state appear better than a baseline that ignores the perturbation; against cells from another transduction, most fall below it. Reproducibility should be judged across separate transductions.

items.title_en: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
items.abstract_en: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

items.title_en: Computational De Novo Design of Miniprotein Candidate Neutralizers Targeting the IL-23 Cytokine Subunit p19
items.abstract_en: Interleukin-23 (IL-23) drives T-helper-17 inflammation underlying inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis; anti-p19 antibodies are clinically effective but large, costly, and injectable. De novo miniproteins are an attractive alternative, yet published designs target the IL-23 receptor; the IL-23 cytokine itself has not been addressed. A further obstacle is that the standard confidence score (ipTM) tracks construct length rather than interface quality. We computationally design miniprotein binders against the IL-23R-binding face of p19 (PDB 3DUH) and score every design with ipSAE, a length-robust interface metric derived from AlphaFold-initial-guess predicted aligned error. A conventional RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN/ColabFold pipeline yields no reliable predicted interface across 972 designs (best ipSAE 0.30), and a scoring artifact, in which single-sequence ColabFold under-rates binder pLDDT by approximately 56 points, explains an earlier misleading "binders do not fold" signal. An interface-optimized hallucination method (BindCraft), scored identically, yields 42 of 50 designs above ipSAE 0.60 (best 0.804). An AlphaFold-independent geometric check reproduces the conventional failure: no top-ranked conventional design reaches the buried area or interface hydrogen-bond count of the weakest lead. Five all-alpha-helical leads (72-104 residues) collectively engage all six targeted hotspots; two dock within the intact p40/p19 heterodimer and all show favorable Rosetta energetics. A p40-alone counter-screen returns ipSAE 0.00 for all five, indicating no spurious p40 interface. To our knowledge, these are the first computationally proposed de novo miniprotein candidates designed to occlude the IL-23R-binding face of IL-23 p19. All results require experimental validation.

items.title_en: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
items.title_zh: 用于收缩期肌肉细胞无标记成像的视频速率定量相位与偏振成像（QP2I）
items.abstract_en: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) has become a standard approach for label-free microscopy of transparent specimens, mapping the optical path length. However, the isotropic phase is blind to the molecular order underlying optical anisotropy. Implementations that also add quantitative contrast to birefringence, rely on multi-frame illumination or polarization-state scanning, or on dedicated interferometric hardware, that trade away acquisition speed or the simplicity of a standard microscope. We present Quantitative Phase and Polarimetric Imaging (QP2I), a computational imaging framework that converts a standard differential interference contrast (DIC) microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate, dual-contrast imaging system. We developed a new globally regularized phase reconstruction that eliminates artifacts of prior DIC-to-QPI approaches, providing quantitative phase information and used per-pixel Stokes-based reconstruction to obtain quantitative anisotropic retardance. We validate the approach across simulations, static reference targets, fixed muscle tissue and living dynamically moving cells. Thereby, QP2I enables to study contractile dynamics in live cardiomyocytes all-optically and label-free. It provides both structural and functional readouts at frame rates that are sufficient to temporally resolve fast cardiomyocyte contractions. While conventional fluorescent labels bleach out over time, perturb physiology, and preclude long-term monitoring, QP2I provides similar established structural readouts, such as frame-by-frame sarcomere length, as well as previously inaccessible measurements, like quantitative analysis of retardance changes during muscle contraction, as a direct optical signature of muscle photoelasticity. QP2I thus enables long-term, label-free interrogation of dynamic cellular processes at quantitative contrast.
items.abstract_zh: 定量相位成像（QPI）已成为透明样本无标记显微观察的常用手段，可映射光程差，但各向同性的相位对造成光学各向异性的分子有序性并不敏感。现有能同时给出双折射定量对比的方案，往往依赖多帧照明、偏振态扫描或专用干涉硬件，牺牲了成像速度或标准显微镜的简便性。我们提出定量相位与偏振成像（QP2I）：一种把配备偏振相机的标准微分干涉相衬（DIC）显微镜转化为单帧、视频速率双对比成像系统的计算成像框架。我们发展了新的全局正则化相位重建，消除了以往 DIC 转 QPI 方法的伪影，给出定量相位，并用逐像素 Stokes 重建获得定量各向异性延迟。该方法经仿真、静态参考样品、固定肌肉组织与活体运动细胞验证，可全光学、无标记地研究活体心肌细胞的收缩动力学，在足以分辨快速收缩的帧率下同时提供结构与功能信息。相比会漂白、扰动生理并妨碍长期监测的荧光标记，QP2I 既能给出逐帧肌节长度等结构指标，也能获得此前难以测量的肌肉收缩过程中延迟变化，作为肌肉光弹性的直接光学特征。
items.highlight_zh: 把普通 DIC 显微镜＋偏振相机变成单帧视频速率双对比定量成像
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：观察活细胞通常要染色或加荧光标记，但标记会漂白、干扰细胞生理，也难以长时间连续监测。定量相位成像（QPI）能无标记地看透明样本，但它测的是各向同性的光程差，看不到分子排列的有序性（如肌肉纤维的各向异性）；而已有的“相位＋双折射”双对比方法需要多帧照明、扫描偏振或专门干涉光路，速度慢或设备复杂。

方法：作者提出 QP2I 计算成像框架。硬件上只需一台普通的微分干涉相衬（DIC）显微镜加一台偏振相机；算法上，发展了新的全局正则化相位重建，解决了以往把 DIC 图像转成定量相位时的伪影问题，得到定量相位；再用逐像素的 Stokes 参量重建得到定量的延迟（retardance），即各向异性信息。两者在一次曝光中同时获得，达到视频速率。

结果：作者在仿真、静态标准样品、固定肌肉组织和活体运动细胞上做了验证。在活体心肌细胞上，能逐帧测出肌节长度等结构指标，还能测到收缩过程中延迟的变化——这是过去难以获得的、反映肌肉光弹性的直接光学信号，且帧率足以跟上快速收缩。

为何重要：它把一台常见显微镜升级为无标记、单帧、双通道定量的成像工具，既可长期监测而不损伤样本，又同时给出结构与功能读数，为心肌收缩等动态研究提供了实用手段。

items.title_en: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets? Experience Reuse in Molecular Optimization for Agentic Structure-Based Drug Design
items.title_zh: 跨蛋白质口袋迁移了什么？面向智能体式基于结构的药物设计中的分子优化经验复用
items.abstract_en: LLM agents optimize a ligand in a protein pocket by editing it step by step and docking each edit. Recent agents first spend extra dockings probing the complex with controlled edits; guidance induced from these probes is reported to help more than the chemical knowledge the model already carries. The probes are then discarded with the instance that produced them, so the obvious next step is to keep them in an experience base, letting a new pocket inherit what earlier ones already paid for. Such a base is read through a \emph{key}: the record properties under which past edits are pooled and a new one is looked up. Using the full log of one such run over the CrossDocked2020 test-set pockets, we ask whether its keys recur on a pocket the base has never seen and still separate improving from worsening edits. \crchange{Using} the contacts at the site being edited, the action, and the round as \crchange{a} key, the base separates them sharply. Within our analysis, this separation is largely explained by how much the edit changed the molecule's size, the action, and the round, none of which describes the target. That is not because the target is irrelevant: naming it outright separates them several times more sharply. For a pocket absent from the base, transfer must rely on a description rather than its identity. Among the exact-match descriptions we evaluate, the more specific ones rarely recur, whereas the coarser ones provide little separation; the signals that do transfer primarily describe the edit and the molecule it produced rather than the target. Under the representations and lookup scheme studied here, an experience base may be more useful for prioritizing an agent's own proposals for docking than for directly prescribing what to build.

items.title_en: Estimation of the Cyclopean Eye from Binocular Free Visual Explorations
items.abstract_en: Binocular video-oculography records separate signals for each eye, yet human visual processing and oculomotor control operate relative to a single, virtual cyclopean eye. This study addresses the estimation of the cyclopean eye during binocular free visual exploration, a target-free paradigm widely used for the screening of neurological disorders.
